content_units: 10-Hour In-Flight Entertainment Mix

This catalog is tuned for a long-haul cabin with mixed passenger needs: easy-start titles, low-friction viewing, broad age appeal, and a balance of comfort, curiosity, and calm. The mix avoids heavy explicit content and leans toward warm, accessible, and culturally varied picks.
24-Item Balanced Catalog
Category   Title   Why it fits onboard
Film   Paddington 2   Gentle humor, family-safe, uplifting, and easy for all ages to enjoy.
Film   The Intern   Light, warm workplace comedy-drama that works well for business and leisure travelers.
Film   Hidden Figures   Inspiring, broadly appealing, and suitable for mixed-age audiences.
Film   Chef   Food, travel, and family themes make it easygoing and rewatchable.
Film   The Secret Life of Walter Mitty   Visually engaging, optimistic, and ideal for long-flight escapism.
Film   Finding Forrester   Thoughtful and character-driven without being too intense.
Film   My Neighbor Totoro   Calm, iconic animation with cross-generational appeal.
Film   Whale Rider   Strong cultural perspective, emotional but accessible, and low on explicit content.
TV Series   Planet Earth II   Stunning visuals and episode-based viewing for easy dipping in and out.
TV Series   Modern Family   Familiar, light comedy in short episodes; easy to pause and resume.
TV Series   The Great British Bake Off   Relaxing, friendly competition with wide demographic appeal.
TV Series   Somebody Feed Phil   Travel-food format feels international, warm, and easygoing.
TV Series   All Creatures Great and Small   Comfort viewing with gentle pacing for older passengers and tired travelers.
TV Series   Abbott Elementary   Smart but accessible comedy with short episodes and low barrier to entry.
Documentary   Free Solo   Tense but clean, visually gripping, and compelling in documentary form.
Documentary   Jiro Dreams of Sushi   Elegant, focused, and culturally rich without requiring full concentration.
Documentary   Our Planet   Nature storytelling that works for families and casual viewers alike.
Documentary   He Named Me Malala   Inspiring, global, and conversation-worthy without being too heavy.
Kids   Bluey   Short, delightful episodes that also entertain parents.
Kids   Shaun the Sheep   Minimal dialogue makes it ideal for international audiences.
Kids   Octonauts   Educational, upbeat, and very cabin-friendly for younger children.
Audio   Beatles 1   Familiar, upbeat, cross-generational hits that suit many moods.
Audio   Classical Essentials   Calm, nonintrusive listening for rest, reading, or working.
Audio   99% Invisible   Short, intelligent podcast episodes that suit curious business and leisure travelers.
Category-by-Category Programming Logic
Films: comforting variety with wide age range
- The 8 films mix comedy, inspiration, animation, and light drama.
- This helps serve families, solo travelers, and older passengers without skewing too juvenile or too intense.
- Most picks are emotionally positive, easy to follow, and satisfying even if watched in parts.
TV Series: short-form, low-commitment viewing
- The 6 series favor episodic formats over dense serialized plots.
- That makes them ideal for meal interruptions, sleep breaks, or passengers boarding already tired.
- Nature, comedy, baking, and travel also create tonal variety across the cabin.
Documentaries: smart but accessible
- The 4 documentaries cover nature, food craft, human achievement, and global social impact.
- This gives business travelers and older passengers stronger nonfiction choices without making the catalog feel heavy.
- All four are engaging even for viewers who may not finish the full feature.
Kids options: reliable cabin calm
- The 3 kids selections are gentle, bright, and globally accessible.
- Short runtimes and low-stress storytelling help children settle in during a long flight.
- Dialogue-light or parent-friendly choices reduce friction for multilingual cabins and shared screens.
Audio: rest, focus, and screen breaks
- The 3 audio picks support different in-flight moods: familiar singalong, quiet concentration, and curious listening.
- Audio is especially useful for passengers who want a break from screens or are trying to sleep between segments.
- This also broadens the catalog for business travelers who may want background listening while working.
Quick Programming Notes
- Prioritize subtitles in multiple languages for all 24 items.
- Offer a “Family Safe” filter and a “Short & Easy” row for faster discovery.
- Sequence the home screen with 3 rails:   Relax  ,   Family Picks  , and   Watch in 30 Minutes  .
